patterns.pattern: Every invoice is linked to a single client/customer entity.
patterns.example_phrasing: Each invoice must be associated with exactly one client or customer account.

patterns.pattern: Invoices and customers belong to companies/organizations, and data is siloed between organizations.
patterns.example_phrasing: Data belonging to one company is never visible to another.

patterns.pattern: Invoice numbering must be unique and follow a defined, sequential pattern.
patterns.example_phrasing: Invoice numbers must be unique and sequential according to pre-defined rules.

patterns.pattern: Invoice has a lifecycle state (e.g., draft, sent, paid) reflecting its current status.
patterns.example_phrasing: Each invoice has a status such as draft, sent, or paid that changes as workflows proceed.

patterns.pattern: Invoice status progression is irreversible beyond certain points (e.g., once sent, cannot revert to draft).
patterns.example_phrasing: Invoices cannot be moved back to draft after being sent or paid.

patterns.pattern: Payment events update invoice status, supporting partial, pending, paid, and overdue states.
patterns.example_phrasing: Partial or full payments change the invoice to partial or paid status, respectively.

patterns.pattern: Automated reminders are only sent for unpaid or overdue invoices, not for paid or draft.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only invoices with pending or overdue status trigger automated reminders.

patterns.pattern: No deletion or archiving operation can result in data loss; data must be recoverable or referencing preserved.
patterns.example_phrasing: No data is lost when archiving or restoring invoices; charge deletions never affect finalized invoices.

patterns.pattern: Credit notes are always linked to invoices and create appropriate reversing/accounting entries.
patterns.example_phrasing: Credit notes must reference specific invoices and their effect must be reflected in accounts.

patterns.pattern: Multiple contacts may be selectable per client for invoice notifications.
patterns.example_phrasing: Each client may have multiple contacts, any of whom can be chosen for invoice communication.

patterns.pattern: Invoices can support both product-based and milestone/service-based partial billing scenarios.
patterns.example_phrasing: Partial or milestone-based invoicing is supported for products or services.

patterns.pattern: Invoice and payment transactions must be registered and traceable (unique keys, external system tracing supported).
patterns.example_phrasing: All payment and invoice transactions are registered and can be referenced via unique keys.

patterns.pattern: Currency handling: invoices may be in customer currency, but accounting entries must be in company base currency.
patterns.example_phrasing: Invoices can use customer currencies, postings are always in company base currency.

patterns.pattern: Advance and down payments are tracked and can be linked/applied to invoices.
patterns.example_phrasing: Down and advance payments are tracked and referenced on invoices.

patterns.pattern: Certain regulatory fields (e.g., VAT, fiscal code) are mandatory for some customers based on configuration or locale.
patterns.example_phrasing: VAT number or local identifiers are required for relevant customers if configuration demands.

patterns.pattern: Plugin/integration data must be isolated, opaque, and referenced by plugin name; payment methods are plugin-scoped.
patterns.example_phrasing: Plugin-specific payment data is opaque and plugin-scoped in the system.

patterns.pattern: Invoices can be created stand-alone or derived from orders, deliveries, or subscription events.
patterns.example_phrasing: Invoices may be independently created or generated from related documents/events.

patterns.pattern: Discounts can be applied at both the item and global invoice level.
patterns.example_phrasing: Discounts support both per-item and global application on invoices.

patterns.pattern: Deleting a charge or payment affects only drafts/future invoices, never those finalized.
patterns.example_phrasing: Deleted charges are removed from draft but not finalized invoices.

patterns.pattern: Pro-forma invoices are informational and must not trigger payment or accounting events.
patterns.example_phrasing: Pro-forma invoices serve communication only and do not request payment or affect books.
